name: Gregory Boyd Penner
current_role: Chairman of Walmart Inc.; controlling owner & CEO, Denver Broncos; founder/general partner, Madrone Capital Partners
profile: Greg Penner (b. 1969), son-in-law of Rob Walton, has chaired Walmart's board since 2015 after ~20 years in Walmart roles incl. CFO of Walmart Japan. He founded Menlo Park investment firm Madrone Capital, StubHub's largest shareholder at its 2025 IPO, and leads the Walton-Penner group that bought the Denver Broncos in 2022.
interesting_fact: He is an avid mountaineer and triathlete who has summited Everest, Denali, Vinson Massif, Ama Dablam and Kilimanjaro.
deep_cut_fact: Before Walmart he was a financial analyst at Goldman Sachs and a general partner of early-stage VC fund Peninsula Capital; at Walmart he started as a store employee before rising to CFO of Walmart Japan.
notes: Walmart press office only answers working journalists. Also in April 2026 he and wife bought a 40% minority stake in the Colorado Rockies (per Wikipedia). Madrone Capital is a possible route for investment-themed outreach.

name: Guo Yingzhi
current_role: Co-founder family member of Kaisa Group (Shenzhen); reported senior advisor to Kaisa since 2015 (current status unconfirmed)
profile: Guo Yingzhi (Kwok Ying Chi) is the younger brother of Kaisa Group founder Kwok Ying Shing; the Kwok brothers held Kaisa through a family trust. He was Kaisa vice-chairman and director 2009-2014, then a senior advisor, and served as chairman/CEO of NYSE-listed Shenzhen developer Nam Tai Property from Jan 2018 to Sept 2020.
interesting_fact: After leaving Kaisa's board he was put in charge of Nam Tai Property, a former electronics maker turned Shenzhen/Wuxi property developer in which Kaisa was the largest shareholder.
notes: Very low public profile; last on Hurun 2009-2012. No personal channels found. Kaisa has been in prolonged debt restructuring, so the company is a weak route. Alive status not confirmed by any recent source.

name: Jin Chengcheng
current_role: Listed by Hurun as owner (with Cheng Sanrong) of auto-parts business 'Huguang'; role not verified
profile: Jin Chengcheng (金成成) appears on Hurun China lists 2020-2026 with wealth from an auto-parts business recorded as 'Huguang', shared with Cheng Sanrong. Searches in English and Chinese did not surface any public profile, company website or press coverage that confirms the company or her/his role.
notes: Could not identify the company behind 'Huguang' (may be an unlisted private firm); recommend checking Hurun's original list entry or Chinese corporate registries (Qichacha/Tianyancha) for the legal entity before outreach.

name: Wang Bin
current_role: Founder, legal representative and CEO, Sichuan Shuyi Catering Management Co. (Shuyi Xianshaocao / 书亦烧仙草 tea chain), Chengdu
profile: Wang Bin (王斌) founded Chengdu-based tea-drink chain Shuyi Xianshaocao, which grew from one shop in 2007 to 5,200+ stores across 32 provinces plus 60+ overseas outlets. In 2022 it raised close to RMB1bn from investors including Tencent, Juewei and Qiaqia Food. In 2025 he set the slogan 'restart the business, dare to innovate' as the chain adjusts after years as China's No. 2 tea chain by scale.
interesting_fact: Shuyi's signature 'shaoxiancao' (grass-jelly) drink sold more than 200 million cups in its peak year and is still the chain's best-seller.
deep_cut_fact: The brand began in 2007 as a single shop called '85°Tea' before being renamed Shuyi Xianshaocao.
notes: Wang says he wants Shuyi to be 'the warmest and most valuable company, not the biggest' (Beijing News, Apr 2025) — a usable quote. No published press/IR email found; private company.

name: Lin Jiyong
current_role: Co-founder and co-controlling shareholder (with Wang Bingkun), De Rucci Healthy Sleep Co. (慕思股份, SZSE: 001323), Dongguan
profile: Lin Jiyong (林集永) co-founded mattress and 'healthy sleep' brand De Rucci with Wang Bingkun in Dongguan in 2004; the two are acting-in-concert controlling shareholders of the Shenzhen-listed company. De Rucci had ~4,200 stores in China by 2020 and reported 2025 revenue of RMB5.23bn.
interesting_fact: De Rucci built one of China's largest mattress retail networks (about 4,200 shops in 2020) plus showcase facilities outside China within ~16 years of founding.
notes: Very low personal profile; Wang Bingkun is the public face of De Rucci. Board secretary has since changed (Yang Nana per 2026 IR records), so verify the IR email is still monitored.

name: Liao Jieyuan
current_role: Founder and chairman, WeDoctor Group (微医, Hangzhou); left the listing-entity board in Jan 2024 but still presented as chairman in 2026
profile: Liao Jieyuan (Jerry Liao) was an early co-founder of iFlytek (1999), then ran telecom venture China Green Line before founding online hospital-booking site Guahao.com in Hangzhou in 2010, renamed WeDoctor in 2015. Backed by Tencent, Hillhouse and Sequoia China, WeDoctor refiled for a Hong Kong IPO in 2025 as an AI healthcare provider; he speaks on AI health agents.
interesting_fact: He switched to healthcare after a nephew spent ~10 months across seven hospitals with two surgeries before a misdiagnosis was found; WeDoctor's first hospital hookup (Huashan Hospital) took six months.
deep_cut_fact: Right after graduating he worked at a forestry research institute before leaving the public sector, then in 1999 helped found iFlytek with Liu Qingfeng and others.
notes: Good fit for a tech/AI angle; frequent conference speaker (World Internet Conference 2026). Dubbed one of the 'Longyan three heroes' with Zhang Yiming and Wang Xing (pedaily). 2018 interview: https://www.asianscientist.com/2018/12/features/wedoctor-jerry-liao-ai-healthcare/

name: Chen Bo
current_role: Chairman and actual controller, Ningxia Jiaze Renewables Corp. (嘉泽新能, SSE: 601619); re-elected chairman of 4th board Feb 2026
profile: Chen Bo (陈波, b. 1971) built Ningxia Jiaze Renewables from Ningxia Jiaze Power Generation into a Shanghai-listed wind and solar power producer and has chaired every board since listing. Earlier he ran Beijing trading, auto-sales and aviation-services businesses. He now pitches Jiaze as an integrated new-energy power supplier and also heads Jinyuan Rongtai Investment Management (Ningxia).
interesting_fact: An energy entrepreneur directly relevant to the podcast: his company develops and operates wind and solar farms in Ningxia, northwest China, and in 2025 he described its shift toward an integrated new-energy power supplier (Shanghai Securities News interview).
deep_cut_fact: His first job was as a salesman at the Longkou Foreign Trade Company in Shandong; he later ran Beijing Yichuan Aviation Service Center before moving into wind power in Ningxia.
notes: Strong energy-podcast fit. Board secretary is now Wang Xiaoyi (appointed Feb 2026); IR email is the company's published disclosure mailbox. Many namesakes (academics) — make sure to specify Jiaze.

name: Ji Yue
current_role: Partner, Sequoia Capital China (now HSG/HongShan), TMT investing; current title not confirmed in 2024-26 sources
profile: Ji Yue (计越) has been a venture investor in China since 1999, working at Walden International, Vertex Management and CIV before joining Sequoia Capital China as a TMT partner. He led or participated in deals including Dianping (Sequoia was its only Series A investor), Ele.me, Tuniu, Ganji, Douban, Noah Wealth and Maple Leaf Education, plus AI-era bets such as 4Paradigm and Sensors Data.
interesting_fact: Sequoia was Dianping's sole Series A investor — a bet Ji Yue was involved in that later became part of Meituan-Dianping.
deep_cut_fact: He said he would rather spend an hour trying a product as a 'novice user' than sit through an hour-long meeting he doesn't understand, and that investors should never be in the spotlight (36Kr Open Day, Shanghai, 2013).
notes: Self-described as preferring to stay out of the spotlight; no personal channels found. A 'Yue Ji' linked to Hongshan sits on GalaxyCore's board per aggregator data (unverified). Best route likely via HSG.

name: Pu Yilong
current_role: Chairman and general manager, Jiangsu Longda Superalloy Co. (隆达股份, SSE STAR: 688231), Wuxi; also acting board secretary
profile: Pu Yilong (浦益龙, b. Feb 1961) turned a Wuxi copper-tube factory he ran from 1994 into Jiangsu Longda Superalloy, a STAR Market-listed maker of cast and wrought high-temperature alloys for aero-engines and gas turbines. He has been chairman/GM since 2004 and is a Jiangsu provincial people's congress deputy.
interesting_fact: Longda's superalloys go into aircraft engines and gas turbines — the same turbine supply chain now in demand for on-site data-center power generation.
deep_cut_fact: He started work in July 1978, aged 17, at the Houqiao construction company in Xishan, rising to engineering-team manager before taking over the Wuxi Longda copper-tube factory in 1994.
notes: Gas-turbine/superalloy angle fits an energy/data-center podcast. He is personally acting as board secretary (2026), so the IR mailbox may reach his office. Source is Longda's 2025 annual report.

name: Huang Xiangmo
current_role: Chairman of the board, Yuhu Group (玉湖集团), focused on Yuhu Cold Chain logistics/trading hubs in China
profile: Huang Xiangmo (黄向墨), a property developer from Guangdong's Chaoshan region, built Yuhu Group in Shenzhen and expanded to Sydney after moving to Australia in 2011. Since 2020 he has pivoted Yuhu to a 'Greater China' cold-chain strategy, with about 10 digitalised cold-chain trading centres opened across China, including a 472-mu park in Jieyang.
interesting_fact: Yuhu Cold Chain's Jieyang park, its second Guangdong project, reported 100% occupancy in its vegetable zone after one year of trial operations.
notes: High-risk/controversial figure: Australia revoked his permanent residency in 2019 on national-security grounds and he has faced Australian tax and political-donation investigations (Wikipedia). Sources on his current business are largely promotional Chinese media. Recommend caution before featuring.

name: Zhou Fuhai
current_role: Chairman (since 2007) and legal representative, Jiangsu Asia-Pacific Light Alloy Technology Co. (APALT / 亚太科技, SZSE: 002540), Wuxi
profile: Zhou Fuhai (周福海, b. 1959) is the founder-chairman and, with Yu Lifen and Zhou Ji, actual controller of APALT, a Wuxi maker of precision aluminium tubes, profiles and bars for car air-conditioning, thermal management and other industrial uses. He has chaired the Shenzhen-listed company since 2007 and briefly also served as GM in 2025.
interesting_fact: APALT makes precision aluminium tubes, profiles and bars used in automotive heat-exchange/air-conditioning and other industrial systems, and is listed in Shenzhen (002540).
deep_cut_fact: From 1990 he ran the Jincheng radiator-tube factory in Wuxi County (later Xishan), and in 2000-2005 was vice-chairman of Wuxi Hydro Aluminium, a Sino-foreign joint venture.
notes: Low public profile; education listed as high school. Email is from a financial-data aggregator listing company disclosure info — confirm against the latest APALT annual report.

profile: Qi Xiuping (祁秀萍) appeared on Hurun China lists 2017-2021 with wealth attributed to a medical business recorded as 'Tairui'. Chinese and English searches found no public profile, filing or press coverage confirming the company or her role.
notes: Could not identify the company. Note: Hunan-based Tairui Medical (oxygen equipment, est. 2007) is credited to founder Ye Zhaohui, so it may be a different 'Tairui'. Check Hurun's original entry or corporate registries before outreach. Off the list since 2021.

name: The Walker family
current_role: Heirs of the late Jack Walker (Walkersteel, Jersey European Airways/Flybe, Blackburn Rovers); wealth held via a family trust structure, reportedly Jersey-linked
profile: Matches the heirs of Blackburn industrialist Jack Walker (1929-2000), who built Walkersteel into Britain's largest steel stockholder, sold it to British Steel in 1990 for a reported £360m, then owned Jersey European Airways (later Flybe) and Blackburn Rovers. The family trust sold its 48.1% Flybe stake in 2013 and Rovers in 2010.
interesting_fact: Walkersteel's sale to British Steel was reported as the highest price ever paid for a private UK company at the time; Jack Walker then funded Blackburn Rovers to the 1994-95 Premier League title.
deep_cut_fact: Jack Walker left school at 13 and took over his late father's back-street sheet-metal business in 1951; Flybe's Exeter head office later named 'Jack Walker House' and the 'New Walker Hangar' in his honour.
notes: Identity is an inference from the list's sector tags (steel, aviation, property) — the Rich List entry does not name individuals. Family members are private; no published contact or family-office channel found. Jack's brother Fred Walker has also died.

name: Robert J Small
current_role: Managing Director, Berkshire Partners (leads its Stockbridge public-equity team); director of TransDigm Group since 2010 (reported Lead Independent Director)
profile: Rob Small joined Boston private-equity firm Berkshire Partners in 1992 after starting at Bain & Co., and has led its Stockbridge public-equity strategy since its 2007 founding. His deals include TransDigm, AmSafe, Hexcel, Electro-Motive Diesel, English Welsh & Scottish Railway and Party City; his TransDigm-linked holdings are valued around $600m+ in SEC insider filings.
interesting_fact: Berkshire's portfolio under his involvement spans rail and power-equipment assets such as Electro-Motive Diesel (locomotive engines) and the UK freight railway EWS, alongside aerospace supplier TransDigm.
deep_cut_fact: He has led Berkshire's Stockbridge team since its founding in 2007; he holds a B.A. from Yale and an MBA from Harvard Business School and began his career at Bain & Co.
notes: Low-profile investor; no personal social accounts found. Lead Independent Director title comes from third-party sites — verify in TransDigm's proxy. Best route is via Berkshire Partners (Boston).

name: Richard Harpin
current_role: Founder, Growth Partner (investor in founder-led UK businesses); owner of Business Leader; HomeServe founder (chairman until 2025)
profile: Sir Richard Harpin co-founded HomeServe in 1993 with a reported £50,000, built it into a FTSE company that bought Checkatrade, and sold it to Brookfield for £4.1bn in 2023, staying chairman until 2025. He now backs founder-led brands via Growth Partner, owns Business Leader and wrote the 2025 bestseller 'How to Make a Billion in Nine Steps'.
interesting_fact: His childhood dream, sparked at age four watching a helicopter land behind a neighbour's wall, was to own one — he later learned to fly and bought a helicopter and a plane.
deep_cut_fact: Aged nine he performed children's magic shows as 'Riccardo, the famous magician of the North' for 50p a show, and at 12 ran a mail-order business selling handmade fishing lures from a shed at his family home in Northumberland.
notes: Very accessible and media-friendly: Sunday Times business columnist, author, mentor to founders — strong podcast candidate. Publisher is Little, Brown (Hachette) — book publicity team is another route.

name: Shan Yinmu
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder (~38%), Hangxiao Steel Structure Co. (杭萧钢构, SSE: 600477), Hangzhou
profile: Shan Yinmu (单银木) is the founder-chairman and actual controller of Hangxiao Steel Structure, a Hangzhou-based builder of steel structures and prefabricated steel-structure buildings that listed in Shanghai in 2003. He still chaired the company's 2026 shareholder meeting and holds roughly 38% of its shares.
interesting_fact: Hangxiao is a listed pioneer of prefabricated ('assembled') steel-structure construction in China, a segment its 2025 interim report said was expanding on policy support.
notes: Low personal media profile. Board secretary changed in Sept 2026 (Wang Saiyan replaced Yao Jianfeng), so use the generic IR mailbox. A family member, Shan Chenbo, also sits on the board.

name: Bao Zhengliang
current_role: Individual shareholder (~2.5%) of Top Choice Medical Investment Co. (通策医疗, SSE: 600763); no executive role found
profile: Bao Zhengliang (鲍正梁) is a long-standing individual shareholder of Hangzhou-based Top Choice Medical, a leading Chinese private dental-hospital chain built on a 'regional flagship hospital + branches' model across Zhejiang. Filings show him holding about 11-12 million shares (2.5-2.7%) in 2025; his wealth peaked with the stock in 2019-2021.
interesting_fact: Top Choice Medical's dental network covers every prefecture-level city in Zhejiang province.
notes: Essentially no public profile; appears only in shareholder registers. Top Choice is chaired by Lü Jianming, not Bao. Unclear whether he is still a top holder (he was trimming shares). Low priority for outreach.

A plausible match is the Gould family behind Southend-on-Sea's Regis Group (letting brand Lifespace, which calls itself the South East's largest private residential landlord), where Peter Edward Gould and other Goulds are directors, but no source explicitly links the Rich List entry to Regis.

name: Yi Xiaogang
current_role: Director and executive president of Sany Heavy Industry (SSE: 600031); director, executive president and chief engineer of Sany Group
profile: Yi Xiaogang (易小刚, b. 1963, Wugang, Hunan) is a hydraulics engineer and early Sany partner of founder Liang Wengen, joining in 1995 after a decade at the Beijing Research Institute of Automation for Machinery Industry. As Sany's long-time chief engineer he led its concrete-pump-truck technology; he remains a Sany Heavy director and executive president.
interesting_fact: For over a year in Sany's early days he and Liang Wengen slept in the work shed to fix the trailer pump; he designed a valve to replace pipe-swapping despite objections that 'foreigners all use pipes'.
deep_cut_fact: He led Sany's ultra-long boom concrete pump truck project, which won a second-class National Technological Invention Award in 2012; he was named a National Outstanding Engineer in January 2024.
notes: Engineer-founder angle; holds a PhD from Chang'an University and is an adjunct professor at HUST. Sany also has a large wind-turbine business (Sany Renewable Energy), relevant for an energy podcast.

name: Ding Jian
current_role: Managing Director, GSR Ventures (金沙江创投); AsiaInfo co-founder and board member
profile: Ding Jian (James Ding, b. 1965, Beijing) co-founded AsiaInfo with Edward Tian in Texas in 1993; the firm helped design and build China's early internet infrastructure and, under his leadership as CEO, became the first Chinese tech company to list on NASDAQ. He later chaired AsiaInfo-Linkage and now invests in early-stage AI, big data, health IT and VR/AR companies at GSR Ventures.
interesting_fact: As AsiaInfo CEO he led the first-ever NASDAQ IPO by a Chinese high-tech company; AsiaInfo played a key role in building China's internet backbone — a natural data-infrastructure angle for the podcast.
deep_cut_fact: His undergraduate degree is in chemistry from Peking University; he then earned an MS in information science at UCLA, and he was AsiaInfo's CTO in its early years (1993-1999).
notes: Strong fit (internet-infrastructure pioneer turned AI investor). His GSR profile publishes a direct email link. Stanford APARC listing: https://aparc.fsi.stanford.edu/node/35179. Long-time Baidu independent director (since 2005, per UCLA JRI bio).
